description.purpose: The agent core as one template (GH #28, R-CG-1/R-CG-2): a hive that references collector@3.4.0 as `collector` and dispatcher@1.1.2 as `dispatcher` plus ONE llm brain slot and the cell that declares the core's own errand, with every internal edge pre-wired - the seam with its own iteration bound and its own restore_ttl, the dispatcher lanes, the loopback. Structurally a talky without a channel: no session-keeper, no summarizer, no proxy, because the core has no channel, no sessions and no night. Its conversation is the errands the channel voices send it. Since 4.1.0 the curator is LIVE here and nowhere else (GH #451): the collector ships with `context_window` set instead of 0, because a cogny is the shape the curator was built for - few turns, huge tool results - while a channel voice is the other one. The `thread_recall` lane it needs comes with it: `./dispatcher -> ./collector` on the reserved tool name, which is the second reserved name the guarded default exit of 4.0.2 was designed to cost exactly one ordinary edge. Without that lane a stub is a dead end, so the two land together or not at all. Since 4.2.0 ([#458](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/458)) the composite carries the lane its own seal made impossible: `in_pack`, from the hive path through the collector into the brain, where a pack of durable `system.*` slots becomes an upsert into its own `cell.db`. It needed `collector@3.2.0` and answers every pack ONCE on `pack_ack`, paired in `required_drains`. Since `4.3.0` ([#464](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/464)) the core asks the tools hive what its tools look like instead of carrying a typed menu: it declares `["*"]` -- a reasoning core should reach everything its surface can, and a list typed here would be a second copy of a catalogue that drifts on the first tool added -- `./menu-clock` ticks, the request leaves on `schemas` and the answer comes back on `in_menu`, written into `./brain` as durable `system.tools`. Since `4.4.0` ([#528](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/528)) the core is the PROBLEM SOLVER and only that, and it costs one cell slot, one lane pair and one knob. ONE brain: `brain_fast`, `escalate_to_deep` and the `consult_class` lookup lane are gone, because the right owner of a fast memory question is the conversation surface that already holds the window -- routing it through an advisor was the round trip GH #124 measured. WHOEVER IS REACHED DECLARES THEMSELVES: `in_schemas` in, `tool_schemas` out, the tools hive's own lane pair and answer shape, carrying exactly one schema -- `consult_cogny` with `question` and `context` both REQUIRED, `eta` and `consult_id` optional -- whose description is the class boundary. Without it the `consult_cogny` declaration had no owner at all after #464 and a grown caller offered its model a menu without the one tool the core exists for. And the memory leg is a TOOL: `memory_call_tier` goes to `"1"` and one ordinary `./dispatcher -> ./collector` edge holds the reserved name, while `memory_tier` stays empty -- a problem solver asks about a time range or a session on purpose and is not handed an ambient bundle it did not ask for. A removed cell slot is a contract change and a new accepted lane is additive; both are the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a). Also in `4.4.0` ([#539](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/539)) the "without a channel" above is enforced instead of merely stated: the dispatcher ships with `interim` off. A thinking model puts a sentence next to its tool bundle -- "I am checking the official fares now" -- and the dispatcher used to send it on the answer lane, which for THIS composite is the advice lane of the voice that asked. So the voice was handed an advisor's answer that was not one, said it to the user, and sometimes consulted again; the core answered with its next interim sentence. Measured on a live colony: 11 of 26 answers on that lane were interim, and one user turn produced thirteen messages. Off, the sentence does not leave the dispatcher at all and does not enter the core's own window either -- a sentence nobody could hear was never said -- while the FINAL answer is untouched. One knob on a ref, no lane and no cell -- and the version does not move, because 4.4.0 is unreleased and an unreleased entry is amended in place.
description.use_when: One per agent, never one per channel voice - a sibling hive of the channel voices at agent level (<agent>/{talky..., cogny, memory, archive}). Instantiate via add_nodes AND wire the consult port pair, the declaration port pair and the tool, memory and error lanes via add_edges IN THE SAME MUTATION; the composite is an island until an edge crosses into it. The ingress edge MUST promote `session_id` into context - the `in_turn` lane declares it, because the core's memory tool asks about sessions. Instantiation needs ctx.model (the THINKING model - a fast channel model there wastes the split); it takes a resolved literal or a MODEL_<ROLE> env token passed verbatim. `ctx.model_fast` is gone since 4.4.0 and an instantiation that still passes it is not refused, it is simply ignored.
description.not_in_scope: No tool cells - the tool set is the per-agent choice and its lanes are wired per instance on hop.tool_name. No session keeper, no summarizer, no proxy, no channel identity, no persona: cogny mints no id, closes no day and speaks to no user. No memory hive either - the recall/in_bundle pair is wired to the central hive from the parent scope, the core only asks. And no errors cell: the brain's failures are put on the error lane by the exit edge, not by a unit of this composite. And no classifier and no second lane since 4.4.0: there is ONE class of errand, so nothing anywhere picks between two. And `in_pack` is not an open write channel into the prompt: four slot names (`identity`, `persona`, `handover`, `instructions` since [#488](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/488)), checked against a constant in the collector, owner off the envelope. Who may OPEN such a lane is decided further out -- the edge is a mutation, and `templates/submit` checks its form while the broker answers the capability `affinity.subscribe` (GH #458). And no tool SCHEMAS of other people's tools: since 4.3.0 this core ASKS for those, which is not the same as owning them -- they live in the tools hive beside the cells they describe (GH #464). The one schema it does own is its OWN errand ([#528](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/528)), which is the same rule read from the other side. And no interim answers since 4.4.0 (#539): this core emits ONE answer per consultation -- the result, or a question back on the same lane under the same `consult_id` -- and never a sentence about the work in progress.
examples: PORTS - Consult ingress, ONE edge since 4.4.0, landing on the hive path with route in_turn: the asking dispatcher's edge on hop.tool_name == 'consult_cogny'. It MUST promote hop.consult_id to context, MUST carry `session_id` in context (the lane declares it), and MUST clear col_phase, otherwise the correlation dies at the next hop and the errand arrives mid-assembly. Advice exit: the hive path on hop.route=='answer' -> the asking voice's collector on lane in_advice, again clearing col_phase. Five further lanes meet at the same path and are wired per instance: tool out / in_tool back for each tool cell (hop.tool_name says which one; `thread_recall` and `memory_recall` are reserved and never leave -- the exit is a guarded DEFAULT edge (GH #283) that a reserved name's own ordinary edge silences), recall out / in_bundle back for the central memory hive - this is where the memory TOOL asks since 4.4.0, and the bundle MUST come back carrying `memory_call_id` - and error out, which the parent MUST drain: a failed inference is normalised onto it by the exit edge itself, because this composite carries no errors cell.

DECLARATION PORT - the second pair, and it is one decision: `./surface -> ./cogny` stamping `in_schemas` with the body `{"tools": ["consult_cogny"]}` (or `["*"]`), and `./cogny -> ./surface` on hop.route=='tool_schemas' into the asker's `in_menu`. The asker's collector cuts this answer together with the tools hive's; both answer in the same provider-neutral `{name, description, parameters}` shape, so neither of them has to know which provider the caller talks to

a consult errand arrives with question AND context -> the core runs its OWN tool round, asking its memory by TOOL where it needs a time range -> the advice leaves on the answer lane under the consult_id it was given, and a fresh turn of the channel voice says it in the channel's own voice
the core cannot answer without knowing more -> the same answer lane carries the question back, the voice puts it in the channel, and the user's reply returns under the SAME consult_id

the tool round outgrows the budget: the collector elides the recoverable payloads of the older rounds, the model calls thread_recall, the ordinary edge on that name keeps the call INSIDE the composite (the guarded default exit never sees it), the collector answers out of its own slate, and the round ends where it began

model.because: the model the brain infers with — a RESOLVED literal, K-H2 lane B
